lines.text: The heater starts off. The target is 20 degrees, and the last reading is 20.
Every new reading is accepted and remembered as the last reading.
If the heater is on and the reading is 2 or more degrees above the target, the heater turns off, and this is announced with the reading.
If the heater is off and the reading is 2 or more degrees below the target, the heater turns on, and this is announced with the reading.
Any other reading leaves the heater as it was. This gap stops the heater flicking on and off.
After a reading, the answer says heating if the heater is now on, and idle if it is now off.
A new target below 10 or above 30 degrees is refused. 10 and 30 themselves are fine.
Setting the target to what it already is, is refused.
Otherwise the target changes, and this is announced with the new target. Changing the target does not switch the heater by itself; the next reading decides.
Asking for the status tells who asked, whether the heater is on, the target, and the last reading. Asking changes nothing.
When more than one reason to refuse applies, the first one in this list is the answer.
